S22.01.needs: a Free or paid account; a question that makes the assistant search the web
S22.01.note: The chip text is the site name, not a fixed word, so the fixed label to look for is the "Sources" button under the answer. Whether a search happens depends on the model's choice.
steps: Sign in and start a new chat.
Type a question about a current topic that needs web search, for example "What is the latest news about <topic>? Include sources." and send it.
When the answer finishes, look inside the answer text for small rounded chips that show a site name (with "+N" if there are more sources).
Click a chip; it opens the source in a new tab.
Compare: the chip names the site, and the chip opens the linked source.
S22.01.where: Ask a question that needs a web search, then look under the answer for the "Sources" button, and look for small source chips inside the answer text

S22.02.needs: a Free or paid account; a desktop browser with a mouse for hover (on a phone, tap behaviour was not verified)
S22.02.note: The preview card has no fixed heading; the card is a hover tooltip built in CitationChip.tsx. Tap behaviour on a phone is not confirmed in the code.
steps: Get an answer with source chips (see S22.01).
Move the mouse over a source chip and wait a moment.
Read the card that appears: title, site name, date and snippet.
Move the mouse away; the card closes. Click the chip only if you want to open the source.
S22.02.where: In an answer with source chips, hover a chip (desktop) to see its preview card; the card shows the source title, site, date and snippet

S22.03.needs: a Free or paid account; an answer that used web search
steps: Get an answer that used web search (see S22.01).
Click the "Sources" button under the answer.
In the panel, check the tab "Sources" is selected, and read the "Citations" and "More" sections.
Each row shows a title, site, date and snippet; click a row to open it in a new tab.
S22.03.where: Under the answer, click the "Sources" button; the Research panel opens with the Sources tab listing Citations and More

S22.05.note: Searched for carousel and image-result rendering. The only carousel found is PlacePhotoCarousel (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/cards/map/PlacePhotoCarousel.tsx), which is for place photos, not web image results. The owner note says the image-search provider is not yet chosen (apps/web/lib/web-search/web-search-providers.json).

S22.08.needs: a Free or paid account; a prompt that makes the assistant create a chart
S22.08.note: The hover behaviour itself is in ChartCanvas.tsx; the code audit's quoted line was not found in the file now, so this was checked by reading the chart components directly.
steps: Type "Make a bar chart of <numbers you choose>" and send.
When the chart card appears, click "Open artifact" (or the chart in the answer).
In the Artifacts panel, look at the chart: move the mouse over bars or points to see values, and check the legend.
Compare with Expected: values show on hover and the legend lists the series.
S22.08.where: Ask the assistant for a chart; the chart appears in the answer, and "Open artifact" opens it in the Artifacts panel

S22.09.needs: a Free or paid account; a chart with more than a few points (for the truncation note)
S22.09.note: The truncation note mentions downloading the JSON for full data, but no JSON download control was found in ChartArtifact.tsx. Use the "Download artifact" control of the Artifacts panel (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx) to check whether it gives the JSON.
steps: Open a chart artifact (see S22.08).
Click "View chart data" below the chart.
Read the table: column headers are series names, rows are the data points.
Click the download control whose label is "Download <chart name> as PNG" to save the image, and compare with the table.
S22.09.where: In a chart artifact, click "View chart data" under the chart to see the table of values; use "Download" to save the chart as PNG

S22.10.needs: production-state: a map tile URL (AGI_MAP_TILE_URL_TEMPLATE) must be set, and the place search needs its provider key
S22.10.note: The owner notes say the tile provider is not chosen yet (apps/web/lib/maps/map-tile-provider.ts:93). The map may not render tiles until it is set.
steps: Type "Find <type of place> near <place name>" and send.
When the map card appears, look for markers on the map.
Click "Open in Google Maps" to check the link opens the search in Google Maps in a new tab.
Compare: the map shows markers for the places found.
S22.10.where: Ask the assistant for a place or map search (for example "Find coffee shops near <place>"); the result shows a map card with markers and an "Open in Google Maps" button

S22.11.needs: production-state: a Google Places key (GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY) with billing; a paid or Free account depending on the plan
S22.11.note: The card's detail fields (rating, hours) were not all confirmed in the source read; the "Directions" link name is only seen in PlacesMapCard.test.tsx, not in the component. Owner must set the key before a live check.
steps: Type a question about a specific place or business and send.
Look for a place card in the answer with the place name and marker on the map.
Click a marker or the place name to see its details.
Compare: the card shows name, rating, address, hours and links.
S22.11.where: Ask for a place or business (for example "Find <business name> and its hours"); the place card appears in the answer

S22.17.needs: a Free or paid account; the assistant must choose the comparison format
S22.17.note: The button text is built from the template "View as {{label}}" with the word "comparison" (MessageFormatCard.tsx:55 and :18); the visible text is "View as comparison".
steps: Type "Compare <product A> and <product B>" and send.
When the answer finishes, click the "View as comparison" button under it.
Read the card: heading "<A> vs <B>" and a table of the two items.
Compare: the items sit side by side and the better one is marked "Winner".
S22.17.where: Ask to compare two products (for example "Compare <product A> and <product B>"); the answer shows a "View as comparison" button that opens a side-by-side card

S22.25.note: The code shows Copy but no send action was found in EmailArtifact.tsx; the "Send" and "Open" parts of Expected are unconfirmed. Search in the file for mailto was not run.
steps: Type "Draft an email to <person> about <topic>" and send.
Click "Open artifact" on the email card.
Check the header shows the subject line, and the body below it.
Click "Copy" and check the button changes to "Copied".
S22.25.where: Ask for an email draft (for example "Draft an email to <person> about <topic>"); the email card appears in the Artifacts panel

S22.28.needs: a Free or paid account; a tool that the app asks permission for
S22.28.note: The generic approval card's deny label was not found in the constants read; "Deny" is confirmed only for the MCP app card. Tool names differ by kind.
steps: Ask the assistant to do something that needs a tool (for example "Run a command that lists files in a folder").
When the approval card appears, read its title and the details (name, value pairs) and the risk label.
Check the buttons: "Allow once" and "Allow for this chat" (and a deny control if shown).
Click "Allow once" and check the card shows the decision and the tool runs.
S22.28.where: A tool that needs permission (for example a shell command or a connector action) shows an approval card in the chat; the buttons are "Allow once" and "Allow for this chat"

S22.29.needs: none beyond a Free or paid account; the assistant decides when to ask
S22.29.note: A dismiss control also exists in ClarifyCard.tsx; its exact visible text was not read.
steps: Ask a vague request so the assistant asks clarifying questions (for example "Plan a trip for me").
Pick an option for each question, or type into the "Other" field if shown.
Check that "Send answers" is enabled only after the required questions are answered.
Click "Send answers" and check the card shows the sending state, then the assistant continues.
S22.29.where: The assistant asks clarifying questions in a card; fill the options or the "Other answer for <question>" field and click "Send answers"

S22.30.needs: a Free or paid account; the assistant must answer with a table
steps: Type "Compare <A> and <B> in a table" and send.
When the table appears in the answer, read the header row and rows.
Click "Expand table" to open it larger.
Click "Copy table" and check the button shows "Table copied".
S22.30.where: Ask for a comparison table (for example "Compare <A> and <B> in a table"); the table appears in the answer with "Expand table" and "Copy table"

S22.31.needs: a Free or paid account; the assistant must write a diagram block
S22.31.note: No separate mind-map control was found; the drawing is the generic Mermaid diagram renderer (MarkdownContent.tsx routes language "mermaid"). Whether the model draws a mind map depends on its output.
steps: Type "Draw a mind map of <topic>" and send.
When the diagram appears in the answer, read the drawn nodes and branches.
Click "Show source" to see the diagram text, then click it again to hide it.
Click "Expand diagram" and check the enlarged diagram opens.
S22.31.where: Ask for a mind map (for example "Draw a mind map of <topic>"); the diagram appears in the answer with "Show source" and "Expand diagram"

S22.32.needs: a Free or paid account; the assistant must write a diagram block
S22.32.note: Same renderer as S22.31; no flowchart-specific control was found.
steps: Type "Draw a flowchart of <process>" and send.
When the diagram appears, read the boxes and arrows.
Click "Show source" to check the diagram text.
Click "Expand diagram" and check it opens larger.
S22.32.where: Ask for a flowchart (for example "Draw a flowchart of <process>"); the diagram appears in the answer with "Show source" and "Expand diagram"

S22.33.needs: a Free or paid account; the assistant must write a diagram block
S22.33.note: Same renderer as S22.31; no timeline-specific control was found.
steps: Type "Draw a timeline of <events>" and send.
When the diagram appears, read the dated events in order.
Click "Show source" to check the diagram text.
Click "Expand diagram" and check it opens larger.
S22.33.where: Ask for a timeline (for example "Draw a timeline of <events>"); the diagram appears in the answer with "Show source" and "Expand diagram"

S22.36.needs: a Free or paid account; the assistant must produce an HTML or React artifact
S22.36.note: Live running of the artifact depends on its type (html or react) and the liveRuntime setting in ArtifactPreview.tsx.
steps: Type "Build an interactive HTML demo of <idea>" and send.
Click "Open artifact" on the card.
In the Artifacts panel, make sure the "Preview" tab is selected, and use the demo (click buttons, type in fields).
Click "Open in new tab" if you want the demo in its own tab, and compare with Expected.
S22.36.where: Ask for an interactive demo (for example "Build an interactive HTML demo of <idea>"); open the artifact and use the "Preview" tab

S22.37.needs: an MCP app connected to the account; a device or permission the app asks for
S22.37.note: Where the MCP app is connected in Settings was not found; search apps/web/features/settings for the MCP section before the test.
steps: Connect an MCP app (its setup location was not confirmed in the code read).
Ask the assistant to use that app's feature.
When the app card asks for access, read the request, then click "Allow once" (or "Deny").
After allowing, check the embedded panel appears in the answer and responds to clicks.
S22.37.where: An MCP app that the chat can use shows a card in the answer; when it asks for access, click "Allow once" or "Deny" and then use the embedded panel

S22.38.needs: a Free or paid account; the assistant must produce an HTML or React artifact
S22.38.note: The expand (fullscreen) control's visible label was not confirmed; it is handled by handleFullscreen in ArtifactPreview.tsx.
steps: Type "Build a small web page for <idea>" and send.
Click "Open artifact" on the card.
Check the "Preview" tab shows the running page; click something on it.
Use "Open in new tab" to open it in its own tab, or use the expand control, and compare with Expected.
S22.38.where: Ask for a generated app or site (for example "Build a small website for <idea>"); open the artifact, then the "Preview" tab shows the live app
